about: A host's whiteboard command list that the pack's verbs match: names, args, flags and refusal meanings, written as a host gives them, with no host code. tests/host_cli.rs holds the pack to it. Every difference says why beside it.

verdicts.same: The pack has it under the host's name, in the host's form.
verdicts.rename: The host's name is another name for the pack verb named here.
verdicts.ruling: Kept different on purpose, for the reason given.
verdicts.not_file: It can't be on a file: it's the host's alone.
verdicts.no_op: A flag a file takes and that changes nothing there.
verdicts.host: A check or a code that is the host's own: target, access, usage or a rate guard.

pack.why: It lists a store's boards. A file is one board, and what sits beside it is the host's.

full.why: It shows inline images and batch ids in full. A file has neither, so the flag is taken and changes nothing.
A file has no inline images or batch ids to shorten, so the flag is taken and changes nothing.

forms.what: Check items' text is searched too.

pack.why: A file holds no history: version control or the live session holds it.

forms.what: A read verb that names every template, with its title.

verbs.name: add

host_sets.at: The host adds on top, as a canvas does: front.

id.why: Refused on both sides, never dropped: the verb mints the id.

z.why: Order is a list in a file, not a number: at says where a new object goes, and order moves it.

verbs.notes: The host gives the type as sticky when none is named. A picture's src takes the format's blob form.

forms.what: An unknown field name or type refuses, by its own code.
id is refused as a field.

pack.why: An alias of add with the type frame.

verbs.name: update

pack.why: --rev is required: the caller names the revision it read, so a file is never last-writer-wins.

verbs.notes: A field given the text null is removed. verbs::flags turns the host's --<field> <text> pairs into set and unset.

forms.what: An unknown field name or type refuses, by its own code.
The text null unsets a field.

pack.why: --rev is required, as for update. A locked object hanging off it goes too, and removed_locked names each one.

host_sets.cascade: true: the host's delete always takes what hangs off the object.

forms.what: Deleting an object that isn't there refuses, by type, naming that it's gone.
A raw del of an object that isn't there changes nothing, and the report says so.

verbs.name: connect
verbs.notes: An anchor fills its end's anchor, auto when none is given. The pack also takes a free point for an end.

verbs.name: template
verbs.notes: The host gives x and y as 0 when they're left out.

bad_field.why: The host's list of eleven reactions is its own: a file's reaction keys are open text of 1 to 32 bytes, which stamps use.

forms.what: With no on or off it toggles the caller's reaction.

verbs.name: vote
verbs.notes: A host reading perPerson 0 as no limit leaves it out of the file: the format refuses 0.

verbs.name: comment
verbs.notes: Placed the same way: x + w - 12, y - 20. The pack also takes a free comment.

pack.why: --rev is required to change the settings. With no flags it reads them, with the rev a change names.

timer.why: A timer isn't kept in a file: its end time is stale once sent. The host refuses it on a file as usage.

forms.what: A read giving the settings and their revision.

pack.why: set, del and meta name a rev: a file is never last-writer-wins.

too_many.why: At most 2,000 ops in one call is the host's rate guard, for files and stores alike. The pack keeps the format's limits.

forms.what: The op names update and delete, and a bare list of ops.

pack.why: Making a file is the host's. The pack's save writes its bytes.
A file's name is its path, which is the host's. Its title is meta's title.

verbs.name: mv

pack.why: No mv in the pack: move takes an offset and brings groups and frames along, and order takes a layer. A host maps its mv to one of them, or drops it.

verbs.notes: Named in the host's plan, not in its command list.

refusals.why: A gone object is the board's own conflict, Conflict::Deleted. read gives none.
An id in use is the board's own conflict, Conflict::Exists.
